findings.title: cook_method column default is :raw_html, breaking all existing posts
findings.body: The migration adds `cook_method` with `default: 1, null: false`, but in `app/models/post.rb` the Enum is declared as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which follows the standard 0-indexed convention (`:regular` = 0, `:raw_html` = 1). Backfilling every existing row to 1 makes every pre-existing post look like `:raw_html`, and `Post#before_save` then sets `cooked = cook(raw, ...)`; for any subsequently edited post, `cook` returns `raw` (Markdown text) instead of the rendered HTML. The default should be `0` (regular), so existing posts continue to use the cooking pipeline until they are explicitly imported with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`.

findings.title: NoMethodError on nil feed content crashes the scheduled job
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `scrub` on `i.content` directly. `NilClass#scrub` does not exist, so whenever an RSS/Atom item is missing a `content` field (which is the common case for items that only carry a `<description>` or `<summary>`) the scheduled job raises `NoMethodError`. The job is `retry: false`, so the failure is permanent; the feed will never be importable. Guard with `i.content.to_s.scrub` (or check `i.content` first) before unescaping.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a valid directive, browsers ignore it
findings.body: The controller sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. `ALLOWALL` is not one of the standardized X-Frame-Options values (DENY / SAMEORIGIN / ALLOW-FROM uri) and browsers ignore unknown values, falling back to whatever default framing policy is in effect. If the host previously sent a stricter value, or modern browsers apply a stricter default, the embed iframe will be blocked cross-origin, defeating the purpose of the embed controller. Use a `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' https://<embeddable-host>` header (or `ALLOW-FROM` plus that host) to actually permit cross-origin framing.

findings.title: PollFeed is run synchronously on every embed retrieval
findings.body: In `perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is on, the retriever invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline for every embed page load. PollFeed fetches and parses the full RSS/ATOM feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` on every item. A busy embeddable page can therefore trigger many redundant full-feed imports. The scheduled job should be allowed to run on its own cadence and the retriever should not invoke it inline; only an explicit per-URL RSS lookup should be performed here.

findings.title: Concurrent imports on the same embed_url race past the blank? check
findings.body: `self.import` first does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` to decide whether to insert, and only then calls `TopicEmbed.create!`. The migration creates a unique index on `embed_url`, but nothing in `import` rescues the duplicate-key exception that arises if a second concurrent job (e.g. two simultaneous loads of the same embeddable URL while retrieve_topic jobs run in parallel) reaches the insertion point. The losing transaction raises, and since the `Topic.transaction` block already ran a real `PostCreator.create`, an orphan topic and first post are left behind with no `TopicEmbed` row. Either guard the insert with the unique index in a single upsert, or rescue `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and re-read the existing record.
